title: CSE hoists a cast shared by `when/then` branches onto every row
verdict: deviation: a guarded strict cast raises when two branches share it (PL-6)
description: A lazy query collects with common-subexpression elimination on. When two expressions share a subexpression, CSE computes it once in a `WITH_COLUMNS` below the projection, on every row. That includes a strict cast inside `when(c).then(...)`: the cast now runs on the rows `c` excludes and raises there, although `when/then` alone masks the branch (polars-exec-when-eager). Two columns `when(x == '1').then(x.cast(Int64) + 1)` and `when(x == '1').then(x.cast(Int64) + 2)` over `x = ['1', 'a']` raise `InvalidOperationError` on both engines; with `comm_subexpr_elim=False` they give `[(2, 3), (None, None)]`, and so does an eager `DataFrame.select`, which skips CSE.
So whether a query raises depends on the optimizer. PL-6 records it upstream.

The docs are silent on common-subexpression elimination: the lazy optimizations guide lists common subplan elimination and leaves it out, and `comm_subexpr_elim` says only that it elides duplicate expressions: a docs gap. The `when` docstring says every branch runs on every row, which documents the CSE outcome; the masking CSE undoes is the undocumented part (PL-13).
No upstream test pins this; it may change between versions.
reference: The reference evaluates a `CASE` branch only on the rows that reach it, so a plan whose casts are guarded by their conditions is error-free; sverify's Polars route collects lazily with CSE on, so such a plan can raise (ST-12, #604).

evidence.note: CSE visits ternary branches outside group-by contexts

provenance.notes: s-when-cse-lazy: raises with CSE on, in-memory and streaming; [(2, 3), (None, None)] with it off. s-when-cse-cast: the eager in-memory run (no CSE) masks; the streaming run (lazy, CSE on) raises. A single when/then with a cast (s-when-masks-cast) masks on both engines.

evidence.note: Select/HStack: the common subexpressions go into a with_columns below the projection, computed on every input row
is_fallible_top_level, used by predicate pushdown; csee.rs never consults it, so a strict cast is a CSE candidate like any other
Warnings: all expressions are computed and filtered afterwards, each must be valid on its own; this documents the CSE outcome, not the masking
the optimizations table omits common subexpression elimination
comm_subexpr_elim: 'Elide duplicate expressions and caches their outputs', silent on errors

provenance.notes: Added to the description: CSE is missing from the optimizations guide's table, and the `when` warning documents the CSE outcome.

evidence.note: test_cse_11958: CSE hoists a subexpression shared by a when condition and its then branch (lazy, both engines in CI); no upstream test of a fallible shared subexpression

evidence.sql: lf = pl.LazyFrame({'x': ['1', 'a']}); q = lf.select(pl.when(pl.col('x') == '1').then(pl.col('x').cast(pl.Int64) + 1).alias('a'), pl.when(pl.col('x') == '1').then(pl.col('x').cast(pl.Int64) + 2).alias('b')); q.collect(engine=e) and q.collect(engine=e, optimizations=pl.QueryOptFlags(comm_subexpr_elim=False)) for e in ('in-memory', 'streaming'); POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64
evidence.observed: with CSE: InvalidOperationError on both engines; without: [(2, 3), (None, None)] on both; a single such column (no shared subexpression): [(2,), (None,)] (Polars 2.1.0, macOS arm64)

evidence.sql: PL-6's repro, collect(engine=e) for e in ('in-memory', 'streaming'), with and without comm_subexpr_elim; POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64
